The stream is lossless. Every sample of the master reaches the player.
The stream is lossy. The codec discarded detail that no later stage can bring back.
The decoder hands on the samples at the depth and rate of the stream.
The decoder hands on fewer bits than the stream carries.
Volume normalization turns the track down with a gain, which changes the samples.
Android sends the stream to the USB device without mixing or resampling it.
Bluetooth compresses the audio again before it reaches the speaker or headphones.
The Android mixer resamples the stream to its own rate before the output.
Android mixes the stream with other sounds and sends it to the output at the rate of the mixer.

An album plays as released. D\'JAI is off for it.

Blends the end of a song into the next one. Albums stay gapless. It plays through the D\'JAI mixer, so bit-perfect output is off while it is on.
This report has the app version, the model of the phone, its Android version and what went wrong. It has nothing else. Share it so that the fault can be found.
Analyzing %1$s for D\'JAI. It takes about a minute.
%1$s is ready: %2$s BPM, key %3$s, %4$d cue points
Turn on D\'JAI to analyze songs
Shows the tempo, key and energy that D\'JAI kept for a song under its name. A G always marks the songs that D\'JAI has kept.
The song that leaves thins out and the song that comes in opens up, as on a mixer.
Rolls a loop over the last two beats before the swap when both songs are loud.
Starts the blend at the outro of a song and enters the next one so that its drop lands on the swap. It needs songs that D\'JAI has heard.
Washes out the song that leaves with an echo when two songs do not match.
Does not lock a straight song on a swung one, and counts the groove in the match.
Prefers a next song that breaks a run of loud songs, or of quiet ones, when it still goes well.
Change the next song below %1$d%% match
When the next song matches the one that plays by less than this, D\'JAI picks a better one from the queue.
How many of the next songs D\'JAI listens to, so that it can choose among them.
%1$d songs have their tempo, key, energy or cue points kept
Removes the tempo, key, energy and cue points of all songs
D\'JAI will listen to the songs again. The songs themselves are not touched.
D\'JAI rolls a loop before the swap and uses the drops and outros that it found in songs it has heard. It does this by itself.
Tints the player, its play button and the spectrum with the main colour of the cover. A cover without colour stays white.
D\'JAI can learn the tempo and the key of the songs ahead without listening to them, so that it can pick a better next song sooner. It still listens, to learn the energy and to place the mix.
D\'JAI only listens to the songs
Tempo and key from the song data that TIDAL already gives. Nothing new is sent.
Also asks Deezer for the tempo, by the ISRC of the song, when TIDAL has none. Only the ISRC is sent.

Keeps the songs you listen to on this device, so that they start at once and use no data when played again. The oldest are removed when the cache is full. D\'JAI also remembers what it learned about each song, so it does not have to listen to it again.
Studio glue, saturation, tape, air and vinyl for the sound. It plays through the D\'JAI mixer, so bit-perfect output is off while it is on. Albums stay free of transitions.
A gentle compressor that holds the mix together
Warm saturation, a softer top end, slow wow and flutter, a faint hiss
Crackle, surface noise and a low rumble
Smooth and even. Holds a whole mix together without drawing attention.
Slow, smooth and warm. The longer it works, the slower it lets go. Good for vocals and soft music.
Very fast and aggressive, with a little grit. Brings drums and energy forward.
Clean, firm and precise. Tightens the mix and keeps the tone as it was.
A tube-like soft knee that stiffens as the level rises. Slow, rich and gentle.
Punchy and thick, with a hint of transformer saturation.
Heavy compression blended under the original. Lifts quiet detail and adds sustain.
Plays the music without the processing, at the same loudness, so that louder is not heard as better
Presses the centre and the sides apart
Transformer warmth: the lows saturate harder
Triode warmth, with the even harmonics of a tube
A soft shine on the top end
Rounds off the peaks instead of cutting them
A clean, steady machine with a full top end.
An older machine: warmer, darker and a little unsteady.
Narrow and hissy, thin in the lows, quick to wobble.
Heavy wobble, a dull top end and small dips in the level.
A clean pressing: a quiet surface and very little crackle.
Steady crackle, and one scratch that comes round at every turn.
A lot of small pops and a noisier surface.
Tone Lab colours the sound on purpose. It can compress, saturate, add tape character, air and vinyl crackle, so the signal is processed.
Mixes each track into the next on the beat, with matched tempo and an EQ hand-over. It plays through its own mixer, so bit-perfect output is off.
D\'JAI plays through its own mixer. The audio is resampled to 48 kHz and handled as floating point. While two tracks blend, the EQ of each one changes, so the signal is processed.
